A1.justification: Both PDFs are complete 15-page versions of the same STAtten paper. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and Appendices A–E are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original STAtten classification experiments, model-capacity comparisons, temporal ablations, and firing-rate measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains original classification and ablation results and additionally reports object-detection, transfer-learning, and ImageNet block-size results.

M1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds a limited architectural adaptation by replacing the EMS-YOLO backbone with STAtten for detection. The core block-wise attention computation and existing transformer integrations in Sections 4.2–4.3 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Appendix D.1 newly evaluates PASCAL VOC object detection, substantially extending coverage from classification to object localization on a new dataset. Existing static, sequential, and neuromorphic coverage remains. The transfer experiments reuse CIFAR10/100 rather than adding another dataset.

E2.justification: Table 11 introduces Spiking-YOLO as a comparator alongside SDT. Table 12 uses the already represented Spikformer and SpikingReformer methods. The earlier Spikformer/QKFormer training-curve comparison is removed, while comparator membership in the retained main benchmark tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: New evaluation regimes include transfer using ImageNet-pretrained weights and 224×224 CIFAR inputs, and VOC detection measured by mAP@0.5 and mAP@0.5:0.9. Separately, Figure 5 revises the reported model-size grid from 2.56/5.79/7.07/10.23M to 2.56/5.79/10.23/22.97M, and Table 10 adds ImageNet testing with T=4 and B=1/2/4. Table 8's existing training settings remain unchanged; these additions do not establish that the retained experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix C.2 extends the existing block-size sensitivity analysis to ImageNet, and Figure 5 revises the model-capacity sweep. Conversely, v2's Appendix D and Figure 6 analysis of the first ten ImageNet training epochs is removed. The entropy, neuron-activity, and timestep-combination analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version supplies repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. The new tables continue the existing point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: New Tables 11–12 report STAtten+SDT detection scores of 52.98/27.53 on the two mAP metrics and transfer accuracies of 97.76/86.67 on CIFAR10/100. Table 10 adds ImageNet accuracies of 77.65/78.00/78.06 for B=1/2/4. With its revised size grid, Figure 5 and Section 5.4 change reported accuracy advantages from approximately 1–1.5 to 0.5–1.0 percentage points on CIFAR100 and 3–6 to 3–5 on sequential CIFAR100. Earlier training-curve results are removed; main Tables 2–6 retain their values.

T1.justification: Equations 1–19, the attention definitions, complexity and energy expressions, and Appendix C.1's binary-matrix examples are unchanged. No new or revised formal assumptions, proofs, or derivations are introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution statements, and conclusion retain the same central claims about block-wise spatial-temporal attention, plug-and-play integration, computational complexity, and improved static and neuromorphic performance. The appended applications add supporting evidence without redefining those contributions.

C2.justification: Appendix C.2 adds a general interpretation linking optimal block size to the temporal-to-spatial information ratio, while new Appendix D interprets detection and transfer results as broader generalizability. Section 5.5 replaces proposed video-task extensions with a more specific discussion of layer-by-layer hardware and parallel LIF neurons. The earlier training-curve interpretation is removed.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code repository URL. Appendix D supplies basic detector-integration information, a pointer to the baseline training configuration, and the pretrained-weight and resizing choices for transfer. Existing hyperparameters, hardware specifications, and energy-calculation details in Appendices A–B remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references covering VOC, Spiking-YOLO, temporal information dynamics, parallel neurons, SATA, pruning, quantization, and ReSpike. Section 4.1's unresolved citation placeholder is replaced with a citation to the temporal-information study. The principal positioning against spatial-only spiking transformers remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Rewriting is localized to the capacity and limitations discussions, expanded Appendix C.2, and replacement of Appendix D with two application subsections. A code sentence and acknowledgment are added. The overall organization and most introductory, methodological, and concluding prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 5 is redrawn and relocated, with changed parameter-axis labels and plot ranges. Figure 6 is removed; Table 10 is expanded, relocated, and reordered; Tables 11–12 are added. These changes are localized within the retained two-column layout.

improvement.justification: The new VOC evaluation and ImageNet block-size sweep provide useful additional evidence for applicability and block selection, while the repository link improves access information. The gains are limited: early ImageNet training curves are removed, new protocols are briefly documented, and the transfer comparison lacks an SDT-only control. Appendix D.2's pretrained transfer also conflicts with Section 5's retained blanket statement that all models are trained from scratch. Overall, the added support provides a modest improvement.
